question.text: Mr. Ashwin Nair (Manager, Mahi Fund) explains to an LP that his fund has two tiers: 'super key persons' and 'standard key persons'. Per Ch 12, this structure is typically used when:

answer.text: The fund has multiple founders/partners, where senior partners handle capital/investor relationships (super key) while others oversee fund management (standard key), and additional senior investment-team executives are bracketed as standard key.
SEBI mandates the two-tier structure for all Category I and II AIFs.
Only the Sponsor can be a 'super key' person.
The two-tier structure allows the fund to avoid the Key-Man clause entirely.

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 12 gives the four-founders example — two senior are super key persons (capital/investor relationships), two junior are standard key persons (fund management), and additional transaction-team leaders/reporting leads may be 'standard key' too. The Trap: B is fabricated SEBI rule. C is wrong — Sponsors are a separate regulatory construct. D inverts reality — structure exists WITHIN the Key-Man framework, it doesn't avoid it. Cross-Exam Context: Concept similar to 'principal' vs 'associate' designations in XXI-B (PM) but with carry implications unique to AIF. Manager's Pro-Tip: The two-tier structure helps you negotiate a less punitive Key-Man trigger — e.g., only a 'super key' departure triggers investment suspension, while a 'standard key' departure just requires replacement within 90 days.
